Triage: `pm:blocked` + `domain:ui` + `bug`.

Blocked-by: #6110

Rationale: real asymmetry with a fail-open consequence — a `features.*` predicate faults on `/forms/:name` and `visibleWhen` defaults visible: one authored text, two verdicts, the same class as #6110 itself one scope root over. Same route component as in-flight PR #6261 ⇒ blocked behind #6110; on its close re-verify on the merged ref (the gap is recorded in `FormPage.tsx`'s own comment there).

Not P0: unmeasured whether any shipped form-view metadata authors `features.*` — measuring that is the claim's first step. Fork clause: if nothing does and the honest fix becomes "form views may not name `features` at all", that is a contract question — stop and send back to triage instead of wiring. Otherwise this stays a wiring fix: fill `features` from `getAuthConfig()` following `AppContent`'s own pattern — `ExpressionProvider` already documents `{}` as the deliberate pre-load state, so matching in-app semantics (not inventing stricter pre-load behaviour) keeps parity the goal.

## Unlock scan + the card's own open measurement, now taken — `pm:blocked` → `pm:queue` **+ `pm:retriage`**

`domain:ui` @ objectui execution seat, PM session `session_011SfZeFWrhGLHmfq61xbz4q`. Labels moved in one stroke; `pm:retriage` is attached **alongside**, ⛔ nothing removed but the discharged `pm:blocked`.

### 1. The block is discharged — and it was never going to discharge itself

`Blocked-by: #6110` (recorded in a comment on this card, not the body). **#6110 closed 2026-08-25T06:35:50Z** — 7½ hours before this reading — and nothing returned this card to the queue. It sat `pm:blocked` on a closed upstream, which is the state that makes a card permanently invisible to the Bug-first order.

⚠️ **Worth recording for the lane:** three of the four `pm:blocked` Bugs in `domain:ui` carry **no `Blocked-by:` line in the body**. This repo's convention puts them in comments — a body-only grep reports "no blocker" for cards that plainly have one, and I nearly filed that as a finding before checking the comments. Any unlock sweep here must read comments as well as bodies.

### 2. ⛔ Do NOT dispatch this as a wiring fix — the card's own unmeasured question is now measured

The body's "Not yet measured" section is the load-bearing one:

> Whether any shipped form-view metadata actually authors a `features.*` predicate. If nothing does, this is a latent asymmetry rather than a live break, and the honest fix may be to decide that form views may not name `features` at all — **which is a contract question, not a wiring one**.

**Measured on `origin/main` @ `c38162d7c`, across `apps/` `examples/` `content/` over `.json` / `.yml` / `.yaml` / `.mdx`:**

| probe | reading |
|---|---|
| **control** — do authored `visibleWhen` predicates exist in this population at all? | **18 occurrences.** The search finds authored predicates ✅ |
| **target** — any authored predicate naming `features.*`? | **3 raw hits, and all three are false positives** ❌ |
| **control 2** — is `features.` findable at all with this pattern? | yes, many hits under `packages/` ✅ |

The three target hits, individually:
- `content/docs/utilities/runner.mdx:12` — the English word "features" in a sentence.
- `content/docs/utilities/vscode-extension.mdx:8` — same, English prose.
- `examples/schema-catalog/.../code-preview.json:14` — `data.features.map(...)` **inside a JavaScript source string** being displayed by a code-preview widget. Not a predicate; not even schema.

**So: zero authored `features.*` predicates exist in this repo.** The asymmetry is **latent, not a live break** — exactly the branch the card said would change its shape.

### 3. Why `pm:retriage` rather than a dispatch

Dispatching the wiring fix would mean building an `/auth/config` fetch on a route that makes none, **plus** deciding what a predicate sees before that fetch resolves — the card notes `ExpressionProvider` documents `{}` as the deliberate pre-load state, so a naive fetch introduces a visible-then-hidden flash on every load of this route. That is real machinery, and the measurement above says it would serve **zero current consumers**.

The card's own preferred alternative — form views may not name `features` at all — **narrows a public contract's accept set**, which is the maintainer floor, ⛔ not a seat call and ⛔ not mine to grade.

⛔ **I am not re-grading this card.** `pm:queue` is restored because the block is genuinely discharged; `pm:retriage` is attached because the measurement that the card itself said would decide its class has now come in and points away from `Bug`/wiring. Triage's call, with the evidence above as input. The `pm:queue` + `pm:retriage` pair is the designed combination here: visible to the right queue, ⛔ skipped by dispatch while the dissent is open.

## Maintainer ruling recorded — Option B: declared narrowing; the spec half is filed and this card waits on it

Provenance: maintainer, 2026-08-27, PM chat decision-inbox batch 2 (adjudication session `session_01DKWDdUJ2XNRESVVWUvcpnh`), verbatim: 「同意」 — accepting the triage recommendation B (2026-08-25T14:59Z facet block); fallback C not needed.

Ruled: form-view predicates may NOT name `features.*` — the exclusion becomes part of the declared predicate vocabulary for form views, rejected loudly at authoring time, so the latent two-routes-two-verdicts trap dies at the author's desk instead of in front of a user. The measured basis stands: zero authored `features.*` predicates repo-wide (18-hit positive control), so nothing breaks today. ⛔ Option A (parity wiring for zero consumers) is declined.

Execution: the narrowing lands in `packages/spec` — filed as objectstack-ai/objectstack#12665 (fix-at-destination; the spec lane owns that surface; Clause-②: yes since it narrows a published accept set, and the maintainer ruling here is the authority that floor requires). This card records the objectui-side asymmetry and closes when the spec narrowing lands and the exclusion is re-verified on this repo's surfaces.

State: `needs-user-decision` → `pm:blocked`, `Blocked-by: objectstack-ai/objectstack#12665`.

`pm:queue` → `pm:on-hold`. Caught while selecting this card for dispatch; it is not dispatchable yet, and the queue label was saying it is.

**Why the state was wrong.** The 2026-08-28T04:56Z unblock comment is correct that objectstack#12665 is closed and the ruled Option-B narrowing merged in objectstack#12849. But it also states what actually closes this card: *"the refusal reaches objectui through the next released `@objectstack/spec` that carries objectstack#12849"*, and *"Once the dependency is bumped, verify…"*. The work here is a re-verification of a refusal that is not installable on this side yet — there is nothing a dev can measure today.

This lane's rule for cross-repo unlocks is explicit that "upstream merged" is not the criterion:

> 跨仓解锁的判据是「消费方可安装」,不是「上游已合并」…… 未发版 ⇒ 转 `pm:on-hold` + `Restart-when:` 加消费方安装面判据,⛔ 不回 `pm:queue` —— 回队烧掉的派发注定以 premise-false 收场。

A dispatch from `pm:queue` would have burned a full dev cycle to arrive at "the dependency isn't bumped, nothing to verify". That is the premise-false ending the rule exists to prevent, and it is the second time today this lane has been saved by reading a thread to its last comment rather than trusting the label.

**Restart-when:** `@objectstack/spec` as resolved by this repo's lockfile refuses a form-view predicate naming the `features.` root at the authoring/publish door — i.e. the installed package rejects it, not merely that objectstack#12849 is merged. The probe is an install-surface one: against the installed `@objectstack/spec`, author a form-view `visibleWhen` naming `features.*` and confirm it is refused; a positive control in the same shape (an authored predicate that must still pass) proves the probe is live rather than blind.

The version bump itself is a human/release action, so this hold has a real firing condition rather than an open-ended wait.

**Everything measured stays measured — the restart needs no new analysis.** Zero authored `features.*` form-view predicates repo-wide, re-verified at `origin/main` @ `38a123cac` on 2026-08-28 with an 18-hit positive control on authored `visibleWhen`. Nothing on this side breaks when the narrowing arrives.

**Unchanged on restart:** Option A (parity wiring for zero consumers) stays declined per the maintainer's 2026-08-27 ruling — ⛔ do not revive it. The remaining work when this fires is the three-step verification the 04:56Z comment already spelled out, including pointing `FormPage.tsx`'s PR #6261 gap comment at the contract refusal instead of an open asymmetry.

No re-grading and no `domain:*` change: this is a pm-state correction on a `domain:ui` card by the seat that owns that lane, not a dissent with triage.
